articles.title: Texas man, charged with murder of his wife, escapes to Milan just before trial; Italy delays extradition, seeks formal assurance that there would be no death penalty
articles.summary: US News: 40-year-old Lee Mongerson Gilley, a Texas man charged with killing his pregnant wife, fled to Milan with a fake passport and preferred to be imprisone.
articles.body: 40-year-old Lee Mongerson Gilley, a Texas man charged with killing his pregnant wife, fled to Milan with a fake passport and preferred to be imprisoned in Italy instead of Texas, as the state has the death penalty for the crime he is accused of. The alleged murder took place in 2024, and the trial was scheduled to begin this June. In May, he cut off his ankle monitor and took a flight to Canada and then traveled to Milan with a forged passport. He was arrested in Milan and his fake Belgian passport was easy to detect.Extradition efforts have reached a roadblock as Italy wants an assurance from Texas that they won't give a death sentence to the man as the country does not have death penalty and they don't extradite anyone to any country where they may face death penalty.The 2024 alleged murder caseGilley's pregnant wife Christa Bauer was found unresponsive in bed after Gilley called 911 and said he had discovered her and attempted CPR. She was taken to a hospital and pronounced dead. However, doctors found that the injuries to her face and body were inconsistent with CPR. Court documents cited by prosecutors said a doctor and medical examiner determined that the injuries were consistent with strangulation.Prosecutors alleged Bauer was eight weeks pregnant when she was killed. Two children were also inside the home at the time.Gilley was free on a $1 million bond when he fled to Italy in May.His attorney, Dick DeGuerin, said Italian authorities have asked for a formal assurance from US authorities that Gilley will not face the death penalty if extradited to Texas.“When we spoke, the district attorney's office said it would not seek the death penalty, but it has not filed that formally,” DeGuerin said. “That's what the Italian courts are looking for.”DeGuerin said Italy's legal system does not allow the death penalty or life imprisonment without parole. Italian authorities therefore want confirmation that Gilley would receive a sentence below life without parole if he is convicted in Texas.Gilley has pleaded not guilty and maintains his innocence. His attorney said Gilley contends that Bauer died because of a pre-existing medical condition.The attorney described the case as unusual, saying he had handled cases involving defendants who fled while on bond but had not encountered a situation like this."I fled to avoid being killed. I went to great lengths to escape and seek protection in Italy," Gilley said to NBC News.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Georgia school district defends pulling 'sexually explicit' book depicting child rape amid 'censorship' claims
articles.summary: Cobb County removed Toni Morrison's "The Bluest Eye" over graphic child rape depictions, but PEN America warns that book "censorship" is a slippery slope.
articles.body: A Georgia school district has removed Toni Morrison’s "The Bluest Eye" from its public school libraries, citing graphic depictions of child rape and incest in the award-winning novel. The book joins over 30 other titles removed by Cobb County, Georgia’s second-largest school district, since 2023 as part of an effort to remove sexually explicit material from K-12 media centers. District leaders say the move is intended to protect students and give parents more control over what their kids are exposed to, while free-speech advocates argue the removal amounts to censorship and limits students’ access to literature. "We're no more banning the book than we are banning rated-R movies. It's just that we are removing those with sexually explicit content and allowing our parents to make those decisions for their families," Cobb County Superintendent Chris Ragsdale told Fox News Digital. OREGON SCHOOL COUNSELOR FACES BACKLASH OVER 'CHOSEN FAMILY' BOOK FOR YOUTHS Ragsdale said district colleagues brought the book to his attention because of concerns about excerpts dealing with sexual topics. At a board meeting, Ragsdale read aloud one explicit passage that depicts the rape of an 11-year-old girl by her father. "Both as a father and as a superintendent, I think about a parent having to explain to their sixth-grade daughter after she encounters explicit descriptions of child incest and rape in a book provided at school, without parents' knowledge," Ragsdale said in the book removal announcement posted online. "As the superintendent responsible for the instruction of 100,000 students, I do not have the luxury of making that decision for other parents and their children," he added. The district announced the book would join dozens of others removed from school shelves, including the popular "A Court of Thorns and Roses" series, "The Perks of Being a Wallflower," "Me, Earl, and the Dying Girl," and "Thirteen Reasons Why." The latter was eventually adapted into a Netflix series about a high school girl who dies by suicide. ALASKA STATE FAIR BARS PARENTAL RIGHTS GROUP DUE TO 'EXTREMIST' GROUP DESIGNATION BY FAR-LEFT ORGANIZATION District officials said other works by Toni Morrison remain available in Cobb County schools. The district says its removals target books containing sexually explicit passages. Ragsdale acknowledged the author’s award-winning status, but argued that awards do not mean a book belongs in every K-12 school library. He said books containing sexually explicit material are subject to a separate administrative review process, rather than Georgia’s standard process for parent challenges. The superintendent rejected the characterization of the district’s actions as book banning or censorship. "And there's not a single classroom in our school district that will show a rated R movie during class to students," Ragsdale said. "Same thing for these books that contain sexually explicit material. That needs to be a parental decision made in the parents and the child's house." "One size does not fit all. So we can't just make a cross-the-board decision for parents and expect that every parent is going to agree with that decision," Ragsdale later added. "We want the parents to be able to be empowered to make the decisions that, as parents, they should be able to make." Parental advocacy group Moms for Liberty echoed Ragsdale’s argument, telling Fox News Digital that schools are not required to stock every book and can decide what their students have access to in the school library. "Schools are not required to stock every published work. They already restrict internet access, movies, and other materials for age-appropriateness," said Tina Descovich, Moms for Liberty CEO and co-founder. "The book ‘The Bluest Eye’ went through the Cobb County School District’s review process and the process worked. The community determined that graphic descriptions of the rape and incest of a young girl in a book on shelves accessible to 11-year-old students in school, often without a parent’s knowledge or consent, is not acceptable," Descovich added. "At the end of the day, this is about protecting students and ensuring parents are not blindsided by their child’s assigned reading list," she said. TRUMP ADMINISTRATION TOUTS ‘HARD RESET’ FOR AMERICAN SCHOOLS, VOWS TO PUT PARENTS ‘BACK IN CHARGE’ Kasey Meehan, Freedom to Read Director at PEN America, criticized the decision and said Morrison’s works are often targeted using excerpts that are taken out of the context of the books as a whole. "While that particular part of a book can be really difficult to read and to sit with and grapple with, what we continue to point to is that books are not harmful, censorship is," Meehan told Fox News Digital. "So what we hear time and time again is that books like ‘The Bluest Eye’ and other books that talk about sex, talk about consensual sex, as well as talk about violence and sexual experiences, they help young people gain really profound and necessary literacy around what consent is, what harm is and how to be in relationships that are mutually loving," she later added. Meehan also challenged the district’s argument regarding parental choice, saying district-wide decisions restrict access to books for every student, regardless of age or interest. "Increasingly, we've seen the way in which state laws or politicians or even broadly, district administrators are making decisions that affect the access of books for every student in the district, regardless of age, regardless of interest," Meehan said. "I think we often point to that making these broad, sweeping decisions that restrict access to titles, restrict the freedom to read for every student in that district," she said. "[It] undercuts the professional expertise of educators and librarians who see, of course, the literary merit and value in having that book accessible for young readers." Meehan also warned that what may begin with the removal of a single book could expand to other titles. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "While it may seem like it's one book, censorship is a slippery slope, and it never actually ends with just one book or one title," Meehan said. "Oftentimes, districts that ban one book then continue to remove all kinds of literature from school."

articles.title: Moogdayo face reveal sparks huge X debate after CDawgVA and Ironmouse meeting, MariaGrace joins controversy
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Moogdayo, better known as Moog, has become the center of a huge online discussion after her face reveal went viral following a meeting with CDawgVA an.
articles.body: Moogdayo, better known as Moog, has become the center of a huge online discussion after her face reveal went viral following a meeting with CDawgVA and Ironmouse at VeXpo in the UK. The VTuber and artist shared a photo from the encounter on X on September 19, and the post quickly crossed 19 million views. While many viewers welcomed the creator and shared supportive messages, others mocked her appearance. The reaction pushed CDawgVA to speak out against the negativity. Moog later made it clear that she wanted people to focus on her work rather than her appearance.Moogdayo’s face reveal takes over X after CDawgVA and Ironmouse meetingMoogdayo is a Twitch streamer and artist who describes herself as an “Ice Cream Alien VTuber.” She is known for horror games and has spent more than 188 hours streaming Dead by Daylight. Before the latest viral moment, her Twitch channel had around 1,400 followers.The attention started at VeXpo on September 19. During an IRL broadcast featuring Connor “CDawgVA” Colquhoun and Ironmouse, Moog approached the creators, introduced herself and asked for a photo.CDawgVA also noticed a cardboard cutout of Moog’s virtual character during the meeting.Moog later shared a screenshot from the broadcast on X with the caption:“Haven’t watched the actual VOD yet but… face reveal I guess.”The post quickly spread far beyond her usual audience. It passed 19.3 million views and later moved beyond 20 million.The attention was not entirely positive. Alongside supportive messages, some users made jokes about Moog’s appearance.That led CDawgVA to defend her. He described X as a “hellscape of an app” and said the amount of hate on the platform could feel “suffocating.”“Seeing people make fun of people's appearance on this app is depressing but don't stop putting yourself out there,” CDawgVA wrote.He also reminded people that life outside social media can be very different and encouraged creators not to stop sharing themselves because of online comments.Moog later addressed the sudden attention herself. She said the post had “breached containment” and explained why she normally avoids posting her human self.She also said she was not interested in “pity marketing” and did not want her appearance to become the focus. “I’m just an artist,” she wrote, asking people to enjoy her work instead.MariaGrace sparks another debate over Moogdayo’s appearanceAnother VTuber, MariaGrace, also entered the discussion. Her comments quickly became another major talking point on X.MariaGrace argued that people should be honest instead of giving compliments they do not mean. She said she would not tell someone they were beautiful simply because others expected her to do so.She also criticized the people directly bullying Moog. In a follow-up post, MariaGrace said Moog did not deserve to be bullied and that people calling her ugly were wrong.However, MariaGrace’s comments about VTubers and appearance drew criticism from other users. Some argued that people choose VTubing for many reasons and that appearance is not necessarily connected to why someone uses a virtual avatar.The discussion has now become bigger than Moog’s original face reveal. It has touched on privacy, online anonymity and how creators are treated when they move from a virtual character to appearing as themselves.For Moog, however, the message has remained simple. She wants viewers to focus on her art and content rather than judging her based on a single photo.Her face reveal may have introduced her to millions of new viewers, but the creator has made it clear that she wants her work to be the reason they stay.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 20 nations call for new global body to oversee AI ahead of U.N. Gereral Assembly
articles.summary: Leaders and representatives from 20 countries released a statement Monday afternoon calling for increased oversight of advanced AI systems.
articles.body: Leaders and representatives from 20 countries released a statement Monday afternoon calling for increased oversight of advanced AI systems. The statement, posted by the president of Finland, declares that the rapid pace of AI development and recent episodes of AI systems’ sidestepping safety protocols demand concerted international coordination. “AI must remain under human direction, oversight and control,” the statement reads. “It must be developed and used in line with international law.” Representatives from the U.S., U.K. and China refrained from signing the document. The statement comes a day before the United Nations General Assembly’s high-level general debate kicks off. During the annual event, political and business leaders from around the world descend on New York City for the week to hash out agreements and chart out priorities for the year ahead. Signatories include Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, Kenyan President William Ruto, Netherlands Prime Minister Rob Jetten, Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and South African President Cyril Ramaphosa. Several ministers and other government figures signed the document as well, including Turkey’s Minister of Foreign Affairs Hakan Fidan, and the United Arab Emirates’ Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan. The statement features three main calls to action. First, it asks companies to test their systems for safety issues before they are publicly deployed, and allow independent evaluators to assess the risks from companies’ practices. Second, the countries in the statement request that governments and regional groups develop common safety standards to ensure that countries around the globe can evaluate their models with required scientific expertise. Third, the statement calls for U.N. members to leverage existing international efforts and “explore creating an international institution, able to set standards, enable verification, and convene states when capability thresholds are crossed.” Nick Moes, executive director of AI governance nonprofit The Future Society, commended the initiative and said it was a sign of clear appetite for meaningful AI coordination. “It is great news that this broad range of governments come together to call for an international institution because no government can achieve this alone,” he told NBC News. “But beyond statements, mobilizing diplomatic, political and financial capital will be needed to bring about the change that they agreed is necessary to keep control over frontier AI models,” Moes added. At the General Assembly, AI will take center stage during official discussions and dozens of side events, with leaders aiming to set the AI agenda, secure investment and ensure their countries are relevant in AI debates. The U.N. Security Council and U.S. representatives will hold separate sessions dedicated to AI on Wednesday. Several international efforts dedicated to AI and AI oversight already exist, but they vary in their remit and technological depth. The U.N. hosts the Independent International Scientific Panel on AI, a group of dozens of scientific experts from around the world, in addition to the Global Dialogue on AI Governance, a platform for countries to debate AI regulation and coordination.

articles.title: No median cuts, surface intersections on future high-speed NH corridors: NHAI
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersec.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: New access-controlled high-speed national highway corridors will have no median (divider) openings and no at-grade (surface level) intersections, a move that aims at eliminating conflict points and reducing crashes.It has also been mandated under new NHAI guidelines issued on Monday that these corridors won’t have raised concrete dividers but flush medians — painted centre lanes with thick wire ropes or crash barriers. These will also have advance exit signage at 5 km, 2 km, 1 km and 500 metres to help motorists prepare for lane changes well in advance.The design provisions are aimed at improving safety on access-controlled corridors where cars are allowed to travel at speeds of up to 100 kmph. Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, Ambala-Kotputli corridor and Trans-Haryana corridor are among such highways.NHAI said the guidelines seek to bring uniformity in the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed corridors and ensure consistency in technical standards across projects.“The guidelines will apply to all upcoming four-lane and six-lane greenfield and brownfield access-controlled high-speed national highways,” an NHAI spokesperson said.Officials said eliminating median cuts and surface intersections will prevent dangerous cross movements and wrong-side driving, while standardised signage and geometric design will improve traffic flow and reduce the risk of high-speed crashes on the new generation of national highway corridors.The move is significant as govt has set a target of developing 50,000 km of access-controlled high-speed corridors over the coming years.At present, there are no separate standards governing the planning and design of access-controlled high-speed national highways, except for expressways. The new document fills that gap by laying down dedicated norms for highways that are access-controlled but not classified as expressways.The guidelines also specify lane configuration based on detailed traffic assessment and future traffic projections. Depending on the expected traffic volume and the number of structures such as bridges, flyovers and interchanges, these corridors will have a right of way of 60 metres or 70 metres.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Attorneys for Alex Murdaugh have filed a motion asking a judge to force South Carolina prosecutors to hand over pieces of key forensic evidence, like the unidentified male DNA found under Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails that they say the state crime lab never fully tested. The 93-page filing by Alex Murdaugh's attorneys on Friday seeks the additional DNA and ballistics evidence, along with raw data from a laser scan of the crime scene in Colleton County, South Carolina. MURDAUGH WANTS IDAHO MURDERS DNA DREAM TEAM BEHIND KOHBERGER CASE TO HELP REWRITE SECOND MURDER TRIAL "Every week the State withholds this material is a week taken from the preparation of the defense, and if the delay continues the defense may be forced to seek a continuance that Mr. Murdaugh does not want and that the Court has said it will not grant. Alex Murdaugh's defense team previously requested that DNA evidence from underneath Maggie Murdaugh's fingernails be released to Othram, Inc. After Othram tested the DNA, the defense argued that additional testing is needed to recover a male DNA profile that the defense says the state crime lab found but never fully pursued. articles.title: US man convicted in 2023 shooting of three Palestinian students in Vermont
articles.summary: Jason Eaton faces up to life in prison after a jury rejected his insanity defence.
articles.body:
A jury in the US state of Vermont has convicted a man of attempted murder for shooting three Palestinian college students in 2023, rejecting his defence that he was not guilty by reason of insanity.

Jason Eaton, 51, faces up to life in prison for the attack near the University of Vermont campus in Burlington. It left Hisham Awartani paralysed from the waist down and wounded his friends Tahseen Aliahmad and Kinnan Abdalhamid.

The jury deliberated for several hours on Monday before reaching its verdict after a week-long trial that included testimony from the three men and psychiatric experts called by both the defence and prosecution.

Eaton was ordered jailed pending sentencing, which has yet to be scheduled.

Awartani and Aliahmad, who were sitting in the front row of the courtroom, smiled and hugged people around them as the verdict was read.

Eaton did not dispute that he shot the three men in November 2023 . Instead, his lawyers argued that he should be found not guilty by reason of insanity.

The defence said Eaton was suffering from a delusional psychotic disorder and believed the CIA and Israel’s Mossad were transmitting messages to him through FM radio.

Joshua O’Hara, the supervising attorney at the Chittenden County Public Defender Office, told jurors that Eaton believed the intelligence agencies had enlisted him to “overwatch duty” to protect a Jewish family living across the street and that God was commanding him to act.

Prosecutors rejected the insanity defence, telling jurors that a state psychiatrist had concluded Eaton did not have a mental disease or defect and that the evidence showed he intended to kill the three men.

‘He pulled out a handgun and started shooting’

Awartani, Aliahmad and Abdalhamid, now 23, grew up together in Ramallah in the occupied West Bank before moving to the US for university.

They were visiting Awartani’s grandmother in Burlington over the Thanksgiving holiday when they went for a walk near the University of Vermont campus after dark.

Awartani testified that the friends were smoking cigarettes and speaking a mix of English and Arabic. Two of them were wearing keffiyehs.

He said Eaton was standing on the porch of the apartment building where he lived before approaching the friends without saying anything.

When Eaton was about five to 10 feet (1.5 to three metres) away, Awartani testified, he pulled out a handgun and began shooting.

Awartani, then a student at Brown University, was shot in the chest and left paralysed from the waist down. Aliahmad, who attended Trinity College, was shot in the collarbone, while Abdalhamid, a Haverford College student, was shot in the right buttock.

The shooting prompted calls for a hate crime investigation, but no hate crime charges were filed.

Police later found three shotguns in Eaton’s apartment as well as a Ruger .380-calibre handgun that crime laboratory testing identified as the weapon used in the shooting.

articles.title: Ready for tech transfer of some parts of Super Hercules to India, says Lockheed VP; calls aircraft ‘best option for IAF’ as MTA tender is out
articles.summary: News News: New Delhi: US defence and aerospace major Lockheed Martin is “ready for complete transfer of technologies of some parts of Super Hercules C-130J trans.
articles.body: New Delhi: US defence and aerospace major Lockheed Martin is “ready for complete transfer of technologies of some parts of Super Hercules C-130J transport aircraft” if it wins India’s contract for 60 medium transport aircraft (MTA), the company’s vice-president (strategy & business development, air mobility and maritime missions) Robert Toth told TOI on Monday. He also said that winning the contract “will also give India access to several advanced technologies acquired by the group in areas like defence and aerospace”.In Aug, the defence ministry issued a tender for 60 MTA for the Indian Air Force (IAF) valued at around Rs 1 lakh crore ($10-12 billion). The request for proposal was issued to five Indian entities — Tata Advanced Systems Ltd (partnered with Lockheed Martin, offering C-130J), Mahindra Defence (in a tie-up with Brazil’s Embraer, offering C-390 Millennium), Reliance Defence, Adani Defence and PSU Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL).Speaking to TOI during a joint interview with regional chief executive (Asia and India) William L Blair, Toth said, “I think Super Hercules is the best choice for India as it has been designed for operating in hot and high altitude environments. IAF has already acquired 12 of our aircraft and has been operating them in difficult missions like transporting men and material to the world’s highest battlefield (Ladakh) to the recent Nepal flash floods for providing relief operations to using the aircraft for evacuating Indian nationals from (conflict-hit) Sudan (in 2023).”“IAF has been doing these certified hard missions with C-130J and its fleet has already crossed the milestone of 53,000 flight hours,” he said.The fleet of 12 for IAF has unique configuration as per India’s requirements and has been designed keeping in mind India’s topography, Toth said. “We are willing to provide IAF with 60 advanced Super Hercules (12 in flyaway conditions and 48 made in India) and also upgrade its existing fleet of 12 to the level of the advanced 60 aircraft, thereby taking IAF’s effective fleet of advanced aircraft to 72. Thus, the entire fleet will have the same lifespan,” the Lockheed VP said.On setting up an assembly line in India, Toth said, “We continue to evaluate options to set up a second assembly line in India outside the US. But what is important is that we have been investing in India with our Indian partner Tata Advanced Systems Ltd (TASL) for the last 15 years and developing the defence aerospace ecosystem of Indian private industry.”Blair told TOI, “We are in the process of setting up an MRO facility in Bengaluru to support the C-130J fleet. And that 60 aircraft is a critical mass to set up a production line. Since production began in 2010, Tata Sikorsky Aerospace Limited (TSAL) has delivered 157 aerostructure component sets to the Sikorsky S-92 assembly plant in the US.”Toth said, “With four turboprop engines, C-130J has a better safety record than others and is well suited for high-altitude and short takeoff operations. It has a payload capacity of 22,000kg. More than 560 Super Hercules have been delivered to 28 customers worldwide and the C-130J fleet globally has surpassed 3 million flight hours, much more than any other contender.”“Lockheed has the largest and robust supply chains across the world. In the last 15 years of our partnership with TASL, we have developed a big supply ecosystem within India. Over 500 suppliers, including over 140 MSMEs, feed into our two joint ventures — Tata Lockheed Martin Aerostructures Limited (TLMAL) and Tata Sikorsky Aerospace Limited (TSAL). If we get the MTA contract, this supply chain will only expand in India,” Toth said.“TLMAL has built all empennages (rear of an aircraft that provides stability and control during flight) for C-130J since Dec 2013 and delivered 265 empennages till now,” the Lockheed VP said, adding, “Over $700 million worth of exports have been generated providing over $200 million of revenue for Indian industry.”

articles.title: Oregon student remains stuck in South Korea over mental health episode that caused damage worth $170; he is out of prison but country bans his exit
articles.summary: US News: A 20-year-old engineering student from Portland, Oregon, remained stuck in South Korea months after he was arrested during what his family described a.
articles.body: A 20-year-old engineering student from Portland, Oregon, remained stuck in South Korea months after he was arrested during what his family described as a mental health crisis. Although a South Korean court acquitted him after finding that he lacked criminal responsibility, a prosecutor's appeal and an exit restriction have prevented him from returning to the US, according to KOIN. His family members said they did not expect South Korea to be so harsh on foreigners and US Embassy reportedly said it can't intervene in Korea's internal judicial decisions.The name of the student has not been revealed in detailsThe student, who attends the Oregon Institute of Technology, had travelled to South Korea to study at Jeonbuk National University. His family told KOIN that the programme was not part of an official Oregon Tech exchange.According to his mother, Iris Cox, the student experienced a blackout on June 22. His family said he has autism and a history of epileptic seizures. Security camera footage cited in court documents showed him inside a dentist's office, where he opened packages, took small items and bent a pair of glasses. His family said the resulting damage was about $170.He was arrested on allegations of theft and trespassing and spent about 40 days in jail, much of that time in solitary confinement, according to his mother. She said his psychological condition deteriorated during his incarceration.A South Korean court later acquitted the student, determining that he lacked criminal responsibility for the incident. But prosecutors appealed the decision, leaving the case unresolved.The family says the student was unable to leave South Korea because of an exit ban connected to the ongoing legal proceedings. His family posted bail, and his father is currently staying with him in South Korea.Cox sought help from Oregon Senator Ron Wyden's office. According to KOIN, Wyden's office contacted the US Embassy in Seoul, which said it could not intervene in South Korea's judicial proceedings.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakistan says airstrikes in Afghanistan kill 28 militants; Kabul reports 3 civilians killed
articles.summary: ISLAMABAD — Pakistani fighter jets on Monday struck sites in eastern Afghanistan that Pakistani officials described as suspected militant hideouts.
articles.body: ISLAMABAD — Pakistani fighter jets on Monday struck sites in eastern Afghanistan that Pakistani officials described as suspected militant hideouts. Pakistan said 28 militants were killed, while authorities in Kabul reported at least three civilian deaths. The strikes near the countries’ shared border marked a renewed escalation in tensions, raising the prospect of further cross-border hostilities. They also threatened to complicate mediation efforts by regional powers, including China. The strikes came after Pakistan warned that it could target militants inside Afghanistan following two deadly attacks on Pakistani security forces near the border in recent days. The United Nations Mission in Afghanistan, known by its acronym UNAMA, said in a social media post on X that it had confirmed that “at least three civilians, including a man, a woman and a girl, were killed and four injured in apparent airstrikes” in Afghanistan’s Kunar province in the early hours of Monday. UNAMA said it had documented over 1,100 civilian deaths and injuries in Afghanistan from cross-border violence so far this year. “We reiterate our call for respect for international humanitarian law to prevent civilian casualties,” it added. Escalating tension between Pakistan and Afghanistan Pakistan’s Information Ministry said security forces conducted a planned, intelligence-driven ground operation in the northwest following a series of militant attacks in the country. The operation was followed by “calibrated airstrikes against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organizations responsible for these attacks.” The ministry said in a post on X that the airstrikes killed 28 militants along the Afghan border. Afghanistan’s government said the strikes killed three civilians and wounded four others — a toll confirmed by the UN. Militant attacks targeting Pakistan’s police and security forces have surged in recent years. The escalation follows months of military action. Hundreds of people have been killed in cross-border fighting since February, when Afghanistan launched retaliatory strikes after Pakistan carried out airstrikes inside Afghan territory. Authorities in Islamabad have blamed the Pakistani Taliban and allied militant groups for most of the violence. The Pakistani Taliban are separate from but allied with the Afghan Taliban that returned to power in 2021. Afghanistan vows to respond Afghan government spokesman Zabiullah Mujahid condemned the airstrikes in a post on X and said there would be a response. “We condemn this aggression and oppression, regarding it as a repetition of such crimes. Pakistani military circles have once again committed such a crime to divert attention from their country’s security failures,” he wrote. “The Afghans will give a fitting response to this, God willing.” Afghanistan’s Foreign Ministry summoned Pakistan’s chargé d’affaires in Kabul and lodged a formal protest about the strikes. “The Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan regards these attacks as a clear violation of Afghanistan’s national sovereignty and territorial integrity and condemns them in the strongest terms,” the ministry said in a statement. “The Islamic Emirate once again categorically rejects allegations that recent security incidents in Pakistan originate from Afghan soil.” Afghan deputy government spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat said the strikes occurred around 3 a.m. in Nurgal district of Kunar province and Barmal district of Paktika province. Citing preliminary information, Fitrat said a local resident’s home was struck, killing three family members and wounding four other relatives. Fitrat said strikes in the Rakhah and Tor Kundi areas of Barmal destroyed a shop and an unoccupied house, but caused no casualties. Attacks come after days of violence The strikes came a day after six Pakistani security personnel, including two army officers, were killed in a shootout with militants in Hangu, a district in northwestern Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province near the Afghan border. On Friday, a suicide bomber struck a mosque inside a police compound in the Pakistani city of Kohat. Eight gunmen stormed offices, setting off a 20-hour gunbattle during which at least 21 people, most of them police officers, were killed and more than 100 were wounded, Pakistani officials said. Pakistan calls on Kabul to dismantle militant sanctuaries Pakistan’s Information Ministry warned on Saturday that the country could strike militants inside Afghanistan in response to attacks on Pakistan. It blamed the Kohat attack on militants allegedly based in Afghanistan and accused the Afghan Taliban government of sheltering and supporting groups that carry out attacks in Pakistan. Afghanistan has long denied Pakistan’s claims that it provides shelter or support to militants. “Pakistan has both the will and the capability to eliminate terrorist threats wherever they are,” the ministry said. It also called on Kabul to take “credible, verifiable and sustained measures” to dismantle what Pakistan describes as militant sanctuaries and recruitment and training networks in Afghanistan. No group had claimed responsibility for the attacks in Kohat or Hangu by the time of Monday’s strikes. Suspicion fell on the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP, which has intensified attacks on police and other security forces in Pakistan in recent years. Pakistan has repeatedly accused the Taliban government in Kabul of sheltering TTP leaders and allowing militants to launch cross-border attacks. Afghanistan’s government denies the allegations.

articles.title: MrBeast hits back at criticism over $10 million Ghana village project to combat child labour, says he ‘literally’ supports hometown Greenville after being questioned over overseas spending
articles.summary: Rest of World News: YouTuber and philanthropist MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, has responded to criticism over his latest charitable project in Ghana after .
articles.body: YouTuber and philanthropist MrBeast, whose real name is Jimmy Donaldson, has responded to criticism over his latest charitable project in Ghana after an X user questioned why he was spending nearly $10 million overseas instead of doing more for his hometown of Greenville, North Carolina.Donaldson recently unveiled Abna Dakwa Village in Ghana’s Eastern Region, a nearly $10 million project designed to provide education, healthcare, clean water and economic opportunities to families in cocoa-growing communities affected by child labour. The project was featured in his latest video, which documents the construction of the community.The village includes a school capable of accommodating more than 300 students, 10 homes for teachers, a medical clinic, community marketplace, clean-water infrastructure, solar power systems and agricultural facilities. Students are also set to receive free school meals for five years, with support from The Rockefeller Foundation.MrBeast responds to criticismAs coverage of the Ghana project spread online, one X user questioned why Donaldson was not doing more in Greenville, where he grew up.The user pointed to Greenville’s poverty rate while asking why the YouTuber was directing such a large philanthropic investment to Ghana.Donaldson responded by highlighting the work carried out through his nonprofit, Beast Philanthropy.“I literally do. I have a 501c non profit and have 10s of MILLIONS of meals in America, many in my local community,” he wrote. “If I listed all the philanthropic things we do locally I literally wouldn’t be able to fit it in this tweet.”Beast Pantry has delivered more than 48 million mealsDonaldson’s nonprofit does have a substantial food-assistance operation in Greenville. Beast Philanthropy says its Beast Pantry has delivered more than 48.4 million meals and fed more than 15.8 million individuals. The programme began in Greenville in late 2020 and now serves more than 20 communities across Eastern North Carolina.The organisation currently says it distributes approximately 80,000 meals each month to families in need through its Greenville-based operation and wider network.Beast Philanthropy describes itself as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit founded by Donaldson, with projects spanning food, clean water, healthcare, education and other forms of community support across more than 25 countries.Why MrBeast built the Ghana villageThe Ghana project is focused specifically on child labour in cocoa-growing communities. Beast Philanthropy says its Ghana initiative is working across 11 cocoa-farming communities in the Eastern Region, with education, healthcare, economic support and community investment forming part of its approach.The organisation says its programme currently has more than 10,000 direct beneficiaries and is built around a minimum five-year commitment.The new village is intended to give children access to schooling and families access to services and economic opportunities, reducing the pressures that can push children into hazardous agricultural work.MrBeast's wider philanthropic workThe Ghana project is the latest in a series of large-scale charitable initiatives associated with Donaldson.His Beast Philanthropy operation has supported food distribution, clean-water projects, medical interventions and education programmes. The organisation says it has raised more than $40 million for clean-water access and has impacted more than two million people across its programmes.Donaldson has also been involved in #TeamTrees with YouTuber Mark Rober, a campaign that has resulted in more than 25 million trees being planted, according to Beast Philanthropy. He and Rober later launched #TeamSeas, focused on removing waste from oceans and waterways; Beast Philanthropy currently reports more than 34 million pounds of trash removed.His philanthropic videos have also included funding cataract surgeries and hearing-related medical interventions for people who could not afford treatment.Ghana project draws attention to child labourThe Ghana initiative comes as child labour remains a significant issue in cocoa-growing communities. Beast Philanthropy says its research and programme data indicate that millions of children are engaged in child labour across Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire’s cocoa-growing regions.The organisation says the problem is linked to poverty, fluctuating cocoa prices and limited access to essential services, with some children undertaking hazardous agricultural tasks.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Tourists seeking photos on remote Oregon beach get trapped by tides, spell ‘SOS’ with driftwood
articles.summary: A group of tourists looking for a photo opportunity ended up stranded on the secluded Lost Boy Beach in Tillamook, Oregon, after the tide blocked their way out.
articles.body: A group of tourists looking for a photo opportunity ended up stranded on a secluded beach in Tillamook, Oregon, after the tide blocked their way out, officials said Monday. Volunteer firefighters and rescue teams responded to a 911 call about three people stranded on Lost Boy Beach on Wednesday afternoon, according to Netarts-Oceanside Fire District Chief Jeff McBrayer. Officials were concerned that the the tourists would be at risk for hypothermia due to the winds and temperature. “Typically, we would wait until low tide, but that would have been late at night,” McBrayer told NBC News. “Our water rescue team used a rope system to access the victims, placed them in life vests and assisted them through the surf to safety.” McBrayer did not identify the individuals but described them as “two males, one female” in their 20s. They were evaluated for injuries, but McBrayer said they only had “minor scrapes and bumps.” Photos of the rescue posted to the Netarts-Oceanside Fire District’s Facebook page showed that the group wrote “SOS” on the beach out of what appears to be driftwood. Lost Boy Beach is a remote area only accessible by crossing a sea cave or climbing down rough rocks, according to the Oregonian. An incoming tide can prevent anyone on the beach from leaving, the newspaper reported. The tourists told authorities they were out on the beach seeking a photo opportunity, McBrayer said. He noted that his office has seen an uptick in visitors seeking to make videos to post on social media platforms like TikTok, but he does not know if that is related. He urged that tourists should be aware of the dangerous cliff sides in the area while they are visiting. McBrayer also warned that the region is expecting higher tides in the months to come given that this is an El Niño year. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration warned in May that El Niño, a climate pattern that brings warmer temperatures to the Pacific Ocean, could come with higher tides and coastal flooding in the fall and winter. “We would encourage all visitors to utilize a tide app on their phones and talk to locals before trying to access dangerous areas on the coast,” McBrayer said.

articles.title: Ballyfermot driver jailed after killing Wrexham woman while fleeing police
articles.summary: Lydia La Polla's life was "needlessly cut short, not far from her 25th wedding anniversary", the judge said.
articles.body:
A dangerous driver has been jailed for 13 years after causing the death of a "devoted" mum while he fled police.

Michael Connors went on the run to Ireland after killing Lydia La Polla, 47, in Wrexham in March 2025. He was extradited on an international arrest warrant.

Connors, 28, had been driving at 71mph in a 20mph zone seconds before the crash, which also seriously injured the victim's husband Robert La Polla, 44, and a 16-year-old girl who was a passenger in the car driven by the defendant.

Judge Simon Mills told Mold Crown Court that Lydia's "excellent life was needlessly cut short at the age of 47, not far from her 25th wedding anniversary".

Judge Mills said Connors, who was driving a silver Mercedes, fled the scene in a "cowardly fashion".

"If the defendant has any sense of decency at all, he will carry the weight of what he did until the end of his days," he said.

Judge Mills said Connors should not have been driving the vehicle, as he did not have insurance or a driving licence.

He added: "We don't know whether you were under the influence of cannabis or not. I don't assume you were although four wraps of it were found in the vehicle."

Connors, who was on licence from jail at the time of the crash, had driven across two junctions in two "highly dangerous" manoeuvres.

Judge Mills said it was "simply by chance" that "more people were not killed" as a result of his "dangerous" and "completely selfish actions".

Prosecutor David Mainstone said on 24 March 2025, a police officer spotted the Mercedes and decided to follow it.

Lydia La Polla had been driving a Toyota Yaris when the Mercedes ploughed into the passenger side, causing it to become airborne, roll over and hit a wall.

The Mercedes was still travelling at 63mph at the time of the crash and three passengers were inside. Connors' DNA was found on an airbag and his fingerprint on a can of Red Bull.

In a victim impact statement read out to the court, Robert La Polla said the death of his wife had left him with a "profound sense of loss".

"My life will never be the same again," he wrote. "To say I am heartbroken is an understatement.

"Lydia was a wonderful mother to our children and they absolutely adored her. It breaks my heart to know that their mother won't be there for their weddings, and she won't be there to see them grow up and have children of their own.

"Our close family unit has been shattered into a thousand pieces, and it will never be the same again without Lydia."

Connors, of Landen Road, Ballyfermot, Dublin, admitted causing death by dangerous driving. He also pleaded guilty to causing serious injury by dangerous driving.

As well as his prison sentence, he received an eight-year driving ban with an extended re-test, to run after his release from prison.

Mainstone said Connors had a record for 64 offences, including nine dangerous driving allegations in Ireland. He had nine offences for being uninsured and, in 2021, in Britain, had been sentenced to six years for conspiracy to burgle.

Jane Miller, defending, said: "The defendant appears genuine in his remorse. He's had time to reflect upon his conduct."

articles.title: Andy Burnham says UK to provide Saudi Arabia with 'defensive' support
articles.summary: The prime minister says "defensive air-to-air refuelling" is to be provided following a request from Saudi Arabia, after it faced attacks from the Houthis in Yemen.
articles.body:
Andy Burnham has said the UK will provide "defensive air-to-air refuelling" support for Saudi Arabia, in response to attacks the country has faced from the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

It is understood this is likely to begin in the coming days and will involve a single British aircraft, a Voyager, based out of RAF Akrotiri in Cyprus.

The prime minister said it follows a request from Saudi Arabia for "military support", which he agreed to on the advice of Defence Secretary Wes Streeting and Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband.

Government officials said the offer is "time limited" and likely, in the first instance, to last "for weeks".

The Houthis are locked in a civil war with Yemen's internationally recognised government, which is backed by Saudi Arabia.

In recent days, the Houthis in Yemen say they have carried out drone and ballistic missile attacks on the Saudi capital Riyadh, as well as energy sites on the country's Red Sea coast.

Defensive support is described by UK officials as that which aides Saudi air force jets shooting down incoming Houthi missiles and drones.

The singular Voyager aircraft is part of a core fleet of nine - eight military registered and another civilian registered - on the Royal Air Force (RAF)'s books.

The RAF also has five others available for military recall if needed.

Speaking to reporters travelling with him on the way to the United Nations General Assembly in New York, Burnham linked cost of living pressures to the decision.

"I go back to the point I made about cost-of-living pressures and acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region," he said.

"Because of course Saudi Arabia has been experiencing attacks, is looking at potential further disruption, and we need to keep those pathways open, and hence our agreement to the request."

Shipping routes through the Red Sea are a vital artery of the world economy.

The Houthis recently seized control of the strategic port city of Mokha and Perim Island, a gateway to the Red Sea - a key shipping route used by Saudi Arabia.

In a BBC interview last week , Nato Secretary-General Mark Rutte hinted that European support for Saudi Arabia was likely.

He said: "I would not be surprised if some phone calls were taking place between European allies, 'hey, how are we going to deal with this?'.

"Let's see what happens, and if Nato can help, we will always be helpful."

Energy Minister Martin McCluskey last week told MPs that the UK was "providing air defence support" to Saudi Arabia through the defence partnership that they have, although would not be drawn on questions of operational military activity.

In January 2024, the UK joined the US in launching air strikes against Houthi targets across Yemen.

Then-Prime Minister Rishi Sunak said the UK "acted in self-defence" following the Houthis' targeting of ships, including a Royal Navy warship.

He also said the strikes were "necessary, proportionate, and targeted" to protect lives and commercial shipping.

Further joint air strikes from the UK and US followed in 2024 .

articles.title: Austin ICE shooting sparks fight over Venezuelan illegal immigrant's deportation
articles.summary: LULAC and Rep. Lloyd Doggett are demanding an independent investigation into the shooting and questioning federal officials’ account of the involved shooting in Austin.
articles.body: One of the nation's largest Hispanic civil rights groups called Monday for the Venezuelan illegal immigrant who was shot during an ICE pursuit in Austin to not be deported, arguing he is a key witness in the investigation into officers' use of force. The League of United Latin American Citizens (LULAC) made the statements Monday afternoon after an agent shot and wounded Wilber Rafael Garces Perez during a traffic stop. Garces Perez was hospitalized in serious but stable condition. The shooting sparked protests in Austin and calls from local officials for an independent investigation. "Wilber is a victim of the shooting and the most important witness to it. You do not deport the key witness to your own officers' use of force," LULAC CEO Juan Peruano said. According to Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, the attorney for Garces Perez and his wife, Garces Perez was delivering DoorDash when an "unmarked black truck sideswiped him." ICE SHOOTING ROCKS AUSTIN AS DEMOCRAT DEMANDS BODYCAM VIDEO, INDEPENDENT PROBE She said he did not know the vehicle was operated by ICE and subsequently made a U-turn under the highway before the agents continued to pursue him. "The truck chased him and sideswiped him again. And the agents came out and shot him in the back of the neck and pulled him out of the car," Lincoln-Goldfinch said. Lincoln-Goldfinch also claimed Garces Perez did not receive sufficient medical care, and the bullet remained lodged hours after the shooting. ICE OFFICER PLEADS NOT GUILTY TO LYING ABOUT MINNEAPOLIS SHOOTING INVOLVING VENEZUELAN MAN "We learned that at 4:00 he still had a bullet lodged in his back. He was shot here in his back, and they didn't take the bullet out, and they didn't give him pain medication. And they transferred him to ICE, to a processing center, where he spent the night without a bed," Lincoln-Goldfinch said. "There is absolutely zero justification for having shot him in the back of the neck. And this is why we're calling for a stop to ICE traffic stops. articles.title: Flights at major US airports delayed after cable cut by construction workers
articles.summary: Verizon, which owns the cable, says it is working to repair it "as quickly as possible".
articles.body:
Hundreds of flights have been delayed at major airports in the US after construction workers accidentally cut a cable needed for air traffic control.

Ground stops and delays were issued on Monday afternoon for airports in New York, Pennsylvania, New Jersey and Massachusetts.

Hours later, US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cable had been repaired and airports would resume normal operations, though delays were still expected.

The major east coast disruption came ahead of the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York City on Tuesday, which is expected to be attended by scores of world leaders arriving into New York-area airports.

That includes UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who managed to board his flight before the delays began and was expected to arrive on time.

The delays happened after the damaged cable impacted the Terminal Radar Approach Control system, which is used to guide planes during takeoff and landing, transport officials said.

New Jersey public transportation agency NJ Transit told CBS News, the BBC's US partner, that its construction workers had accidentally severed the line and that markers had been wrongly placed at the digging site.

The BBC has reached out to NJ Transit for comment.

Duffy earlier said the damage was caused by workers from Amtrak, the US national operator of intercity railroad service, who were doing the construction work. This "caused a telecom outage" which forced the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to ground flights, Duffy posted on X.

An Amtrak spokesperson said in a statement, reported by US media, that the incident involved a NJ Transit contractor. Telecommunications company Verizon, which owns the cable, also said it was not responsible.

The severed cable was actually a backup network, and the error was only discovered after the primary circuit failed, according to the head of the FAA, Bryan Bedford.

Newark Liberty International Airport in New Jersey - one of the three major airports that services New York City - was the most heavily impacted by today's air traffic control disruptions, according to flight-tracking website FlightAware.

It reported that 267 departing flights were delayed today, while a further 257 flights destined for Newark were also delayed.

John F Kennedy International Airport and LaGuardia Airport, both in New York, were also affected, as was Philadelphia International Airport.

One passenger, Douglas Tewnion, said he boarded a flight to New York from Edinburgh and that his plane had been diverted to Boston, Massachusetts instead.

He told the BBC that, two hours after his flight was due into New York, he and the other passengers were still "sitting on the same plane, on the tarmac at Boston with no information".

Though "everyone is in good spirits", Tewnion said "it's just a pain" to see two more hours waiting added onto a lengthy flight.

articles.title: Cat reunited with owners - six years after going missing in car crash
articles.summary: Pandora escaped after her owner was involved in a car crash while relocating from Essex to Aberdeenshire.
articles.body:
A pet cat has been reunited with its owners - six years after going missing in a car crash while they were moving house.

Pandora escaped when Billy Bowie was involved in a collision in Perthshire in 2020, while relocating from Essex to Aberdeenshire.

Billy and his wife Mary returned to the scene of the accident to search for their beloved pet - but it wasn't until last month that they learned she had been found.

"There were a lot of very happy tears," Mary said.

The couple had adopted Pandora and sister Ziggy in 2017 as kittens.

They been moving back to their native Scotland from Colchester when the accident happened.

They set off on the drive to Fraserburgh in two vehicles - Billy with Pandora in her cat basket in a van, and Mary in a car with her daughter, grandson and Ziggy.

However, a few hours into the journey, Billy was involved in a serious crash near Errol.

Pandora's cat basket was thrown from their vehicle and she escaped.

"I didn't see the accident as we were a mile or so behind, but obviously it was an enormous shock when we arrived at the scene," Mary recalled.

"The attending paramedics confirmed that - miraculously - Billy wasn't badly hurt.

"When we realised Pandora was missing, we were absolutely distraught. We spent some time looking for her, but because Billy needed to rest and recuperate, we reluctantly had to continue on our journey."

Once the family had settled into their new home - a drive of about two-and-a-half hours from the crash - they resumed the search for Pandora.

"We sent a message to a local Facebook group and there were a few sightings, but no-one was able to catch her," Mary said.

"We also made several trips to Errol, but to no avail."

Fast forward to 2026, and a woman called the Cats Protection charity to report a cat who kept trying to get into her house, so volunteer Fiona Morrison went out to investigate.

"I went to the lady's garden and, to make it easier to scan the cat, I put some food down which she basically inhaled," Fiona said.

"I knew instantly this was a stray rather than a neighbours' cat who had wandered over.

"I scanned for a microchip and was delighted to see that there was one.

"When I entered the details into the chip database, I was relieved to see there was some contact information listed, although slightly surprised that the contact address was in Fraserburgh, quite some distance from Perth."

Mary and her family were celebrating her 62nd birthday on 9 August when Cats Protections called to tell her Pandora had been found.

She described it as the "biggest and best" birthday surprise.

Pandora was taken in by Cats Protection and a few days later the couple travelled to the branch to collect their long-lost cat.

"She immediately responded to her name and she is still very attached to our grandson," Mary said.

"Obviously all that time spent sitting on my daughter's belly when she was pregnant has created a special bond."

She added: "We can't thank Fiona at Cats Protection enough for everything she did to get Pandora home.

"We are also still in touch with the lady who made the initial phone call – we are so grateful to her too.

"I would urge all cat owners to get their cats chipped and to keep their details up to date. You never know, it could lead to your very own miracle."

Volunteer Fiona added: "I have been volunteering for Cats Protection for 26 years.

"But reuniting Pandora with her family has undoubtedly been the highlight for me.

"Everyone was in tears - it was so emotional in the best possible way."

articles.title: Meet Joe Petraro-Hyppolite, 13-year-old Long Island genius with ‘Einstein-level’ IQ set to begin NYU master’s programme after overcoming leukemia and Tourette syndrome
articles.summary: US News: At just 13, Joe Petraro-Hyppolite is preparing to take a giant academic leap that most people make decades later. The Long Island teenager, who says h.
articles.body: At just 13, Joe Petraro-Hyppolite is preparing to take a giant academic leap that most people make decades later. The Long Island teenager, who says he has an IQ of 168, has been accepted into a master’s programme at New York University and is set to begin next fall. His reported IQ is higher than the often-cited estimate of around 160 for Albert Einstein, although Einstein never had a documented IQ test.Petraro-Hyppolite is expected to be less than half the age of the average US student beginning a master’s programme. He is currently completing his undergraduate degree at Louisiana State University and plans to graduate in May next year.‘My IQ is 168’Petraro-Hyppolite told CBS News New York that his IQ is 168. When the reporter described him as a genius, the teenager responded with a touch of humour.“I am not biased, but, yeah, if you say so,” he said.He joked that people often compare him with fictional child geniuses such as Sheldon Cooper and Doogie Howser.His academic record helps explain why he has attracted so much attention. Petraro-Hyppolite scored 1590 on the SAT at just 10 years old and graduated from high school at 11. He is now studying alongside students considerably older than him at LSU.“They shot like a double glance, like, ‘Wait, what?’” he said of the reaction he sometimes gets from classmates.From cancer and Tourette’s to NYUPetraro-Hyppolite’s academic journey has also come alongside significant personal challenges. He was diagnosed with leukemia in September 2021 and has also dealt with Tourette syndrome, which, according to reports, previously resulted in him being placed in special education classes.His mother, Anne Petraro-Hyppolite, said his achievements remain surreal.“It’s just surreal. When he graduated high school so young, it was surreal, but this is ... everything he does is surreal,” she said. “He just loves to learn. He is like a sponge.”‘New doors are opening’Despite his extraordinary academic progress, Petraro-Hyppolite admits that starting a master’s programme at 13 comes with some nerves.“Yeah, I mean, who wouldn’t be?” he said. “But then again, I am also excited, because new doors are opening.”His master’s studies will focus on sports management, with interests in kinesiology and biology. The outlet reported that he could potentially become NYU’s youngest graduate student, although the university is verifying that distinction.‘It’s not like I was shot out the womb’Petraro-Hyppolite also wants people to understand that being gifted does not mean everything comes effortlessly.“It’s not like I was shot out the womb knowing everything I know. I have to learn it once or twice. Then I’ll know,” he said.Outside the classroom, the teenager also spends time helping others. He recently volunteered at a Five Towns nursing home, helping residents get home safely.A future in paleontologyWhile his immediate plans involve completing his undergraduate degree and then beginning his master’s at NYU, Petraro-Hyppolite already has an idea of where he wants his education to eventually take him.He has said he wants to pursue paleontology.If he stays on his current academic path, he could complete his master’s degree at around the same time many teenagers are becoming legally old enough to drive.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Roger Cettina, 59, the Hall of Fame horse racing fan who turned $2 teenage bets into nearly $500,000 and helped rebuild Belmont Park
articles.summary: US News: For Roger Cettina, rebuilding Belmont Park was the kind of opportunity that could only come around once in a lifetime.The 59-year-old senior vice pres.
articles.body: For Roger Cettina, rebuilding Belmont Park was the kind of opportunity that could only come around once in a lifetime.The 59-year-old senior vice president at AECOM Tishman had spent decades as a passionate horse racing fan, making modest $2 and $5 bets as a teenager before becoming a serious competitor in national horseplayer contests. Years later, his love for the sport brought him back to the legendary Long Island racetrack - this time not as a spectator, but as one of the people helping rebuild it.“Our company was lucky enough to get the contract to do this, and it was a once-in-a-lifetime thing,” Cettina told The New York Post ahead of the racetrack’s grand opening.“Like, wow, a horse player like me could actually build the new Belmont Park — someplace that I came so often when I was younger,” he added.From teenage bets to nearly $500,000 in winningsCettina’s fascination with horse racing began while growing up in Tenafly, New Jersey. As a boy, he would spend afternoons at Belmont Park before heading back to New Jersey for night races at the Meadowlands in East Rutherford.His own betting began modestly at 18 and 19, when he would wager just $2 or $5. About 15 years ago, however, he stepped into the world of high-stakes horseplayer competitions, sometimes putting more than $5,000 of his own money into contests.For Cettina, it was never simply about making money. He saw horse racing as an intellectual challenge - something that complemented rather than replaced his construction career.“I enjoyed it. It’s math,” he said. “It’s a puzzle – trying to figure things out, and it’s just something that I totally got into.”That approach paid off spectacularly.In 2013, Cettina finished second in the National Horseplayers Championship, winning $200,000 after competing against hundreds of entries over three days.“There are eight or 900 entries that you’re playing against, and it’s over three days,” he explained.“You bet basically to win and place on 15 races a day from all over the country, and whoever has the highest cumulative total wins.”Cettina missed out on first place by just $1.20. But the runner-up finish still proved hugely lucrative, and his wife Wendy certainly appreciated the prize money, particularly after he bought her a new Lexus.Two years later, Cettina did it again.He finished runner-up in the 2015 championship, collecting another $230,000.“I cashed almost a half a million dollars between the two – and I’ve definitely not put that much money into it,” he said.Cettina also co-owns two horses and credits luck as one ingredient in his success.“You have to be really lucky,” he said.The ‘master’ of horseplayingCettina’s two runner-up finishes made him the only National Horseplayers Championship contestant to finish second more than once.The Daily Racing Form dubbed him “the master” of his craft in 2016. A year later, he was inducted into the NHC Hall of Fame.His results fluctuated in the years that followed, but Cettina estimates that he has made around $300,000 in net profit from horse racing over his lifetime.“Not nearly enough to retire,” he joked. “Not in New York and New Jersey.”So the construction business remained his day job.Cettina worked on major projects including the Goldman Sachs headquarters in Lower Manhattan, renovations to the Javits Center and One and Two Manhattan West near Hudson Yards.But in 2024, an opportunity arrived that combined both of his passions: construction and horse racing.From racing fan to Belmont Park builderCettina became part of the team tasked with reconstructing Nassau County’s iconic racing venue from the ground up.There was, however, one major complication. By then, Cettina had moved roughly 75 miles south to Sea Bright on the Jersey Shore.“I went home and talked to my wife about it because obviously I couldn’t commute,” he recalled.Wendy agreed to the unusual arrangement. Cettina began staying during the week in a friend’s basement in West Hempstead and occasionally at another friend’s home in the Bronx near the Throgs Neck Bridge.“Then I packed my bags – and here I am,” he said.For the next two years, Cettina spent his weekdays working at Belmont Park before heading back to the Jersey Shore on weekends.A dream job for a lifelong fanWorking on the new Belmont Park gave Cettina the rare chance to combine the career he had built with the sport he had loved since childhood.“I don’t know of any other workers that are actually into this like I am,” he said.For someone who once stood at Belmont Park as a teenager placing small bets, the transformation was extraordinary.“It was an unbelievable experience, and the chance for me to build a racetrack was just incredible,” Cettina said.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Manchester to host world leaders at G20 summit in 2027
articles.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was pleased he would be welcoming US President Donald Trump to the city.
articles.body:
World leaders, including Donald Trump, will head to Manchester next year for the G20 leaders' summit.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham, who is the former mayor of Greater Manchester, said he was "really pleased" he would be welcoming the US president to the city.

The G20 summit, an annual gathering of the world's biggest economies, will take place on 27 and 28 November 2027 at the Manchester Central Convention Centre. It will be the largest summit ever held in the city.

Manchester was chosen earlier this year, prior to Burnham becoming prime minister. Downing Street said preparations will now step up, with hundreds of local people expected to be involved.

In June, as it looked likely Burnham would become prime minister, Trump called him "the mayor of a town" .

Burnham told reporters that in the first phone call between the pair, he told the president: "Manchester isn't 'some town'…this is Manchester". He said the "right thing to do" was to laugh about it and "move beyond it".

When he was mayor, Burnham told the Manchester Evening News that he "wouldn't welcome" a visit from the American president.

But on his way to New York, where he will meet Trump for the first time on Tuesday, he said "politicians say things throughout their career, but now the important thing is to focus on the moment you are in".

Speaking to the BBC, Councillor Garry Bridges, the new leader of Manchester City Council, said an event like this would have been "unthinkable a couple of years ago" and that he hoped it would change Trump's perception of Manchester.

The UK has hosted the G20 before, in 2009 in London. The cost of the security operation at the time was estimated at £7.2m.

As well as the summit in Manchester, there will be events across the country next year as the UK takes on the G20 presidency.

The presidency is currently held by the United States, with this year's summit taking place in Miami in December.

The G20 brings together 19 of the world's largest economies, plus representatives from the European Union and the African Union.

It represents about two-thirds of the world's entire population and more than 85% of the world's wealth.

The annual event was first set up in 1999 with the aim of promoting financial stability and cooperation.

articles.title: Courts must not interfere in cop probe: Supreme Court
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said investigation of a crime was the police's exclusive domain and should be left to the investigating agency's di.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court on Monday said investigation of a crime was the police's exclusive domain and should be left to the investigating agency's discretion, and courts should not interfere to decide when a probe should stop.Quashing a Bombay High Court order which had refused to grant an extension of time to file a chargesheet against a Popular Front of India (PFI) member, after which the accused were granted default bail, a bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar said the HC committed an error in not granting more time to the anti-terrorism squad of Mumbai police to complete the probe."Investigation of a crime is the exclusive domain of the police. It is not the jurisdiction of the court to decide when the investigation in a case should stop. It must be left to the discretion of the investigating agency to decide the course of investigation and to proceed in its own manner. The court cannot curtail the statutory powers vested in the police except in an exceptional case on facts or where there is a statutory bar to carry out investigation by the police," the bench said.It added that courts cannot interfere with the statutory right of the police to investigate the circumstances of a cognisable crime and it was the bounden duty of the executive, through the police department, to investigate the offence and bring the offender to book."The probe agency sought time to analyse how data retrieved from mobiles, computers and other gadgets seized from the accused connect them with the terrorist activities intended to undermine the sovereignty of India. The agency is also required to indicate how the flow of money in the bank accounts of the accused connects them with the terrorist activities."
